title: Total influence under a switching bound
statement: Assume that for every dimension $N$, every positive width $w$, every Boolean function $f:\{−1,1\}^N\to\{−1,1\}$ representable by a DNF or CNF of width at most $w$, and every natural number $k$, the probability that a random restriction with each coordinate fixed with probability $1/(20w)$ leaves $f$ with decision-tree depth at least $k$ is at most $(1/4)^k$. If $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ is computed by a layered circuit of depth $d$, first-layer width at most $w$, and tail size at most $s'$, where tail size is the number of non-output gates in layers after the first, plus one, then $\operatorname{Inf}(f)\le 2w\bigl(20(\lceil\log_2(s'+1)\rceil+2)\bigr)^{d-2}$.
hypotheses_covered: The quarter-switching bound holds for all dimensions, positive widths, qualifying Boolean functions, and natural k
A Boolean function f is computed by a depth circuit
The circuit width is at most w
The tail internal-node count plus one is at most s'
